# Colour

- **Colour is computed on top of the Final Render.** Once the Final Render finishes, one painting's three-band colour is pushed onto the Cuts automatically — it fills in without the director pressing anything. So do not open by offering to grade it. There are only two things to touch: **which painting** and **how strongly**.
- **Re-baking one Cut re-grades that Cut by itself.** It is re-applied with its Scene's sample and strength — it is computation, so it costs nothing, and skipping it leaves that one Cut a different colour from its neighbours. So do not ask about re-grading after re-baking a graded Cut. The re-bake itself is paid and needs the director's confirmation, but the colour rides along and there is nothing to ask.
- **A wrong colour is not a loss.** The ungraded original is kept separately and grading itself calls no model. That is why a Scene's colour is set without confirmation — what the confirmation rule guards against is irreversible waste, and there is none here.
- **A changed colour reaches Cuts already baked — without re-baking, and at no cost.** Change the colour and the server re-grades the finished frames in that range (computation, so it is free). **Do not say a Final Render must be run again** to make it visible — the director pays money they did not owe. It does run behind the scenes, so pass on the response's applies line exactly: it says how many Cuts are being re-graded, or that no finished frame exists yet and the next Final Render will bake with this colour.
- **Pass on handTouched exactly as it returns** — those are the Cuts the director touched again after grading (a regeneration, a touch-up, a version rollback). The default is to re-grade on top of that version, and the overwritten version is kept per Cut so rolling back is free. When the director says to leave those Cuts alone, turn keepHandTouched on and call again — this is not a place to protect them silently or overwrite them silently.
- Read the candidates with list_color_samples when choosing a sample. **You cannot see the painting** — so the ground for what you tell the director is the response's whyItFits line. Do not recite tone numbers (brightness 0.15): that is not something the director can judge. Put the Scene's feeling into mood and the line comes back measured against that feeling, and a painting that was not held is returned as not held — do not hide that and choose it anyway.
- **The light line can be blank (50 of 300).** The commentary did not cover light and nothing was invented there. Do not read a blank line as missing data: describe that sample through its four tone values and the weight and colour of its three bands (shadow, midtone, highlight). Invent light and it stops being criticism and becomes an AI impression, which is the thing the paintings are there to prevent.
- **A Scene is chosen from inside one colour set only.** One anchor painting drops out a set of roughly a hundred samples near it in tone, and a Scene is chosen only from inside that set — the device that lets each Scene differ while the work's tone holds. Give set_scene_color a painting outside the set and nothing changes; the current set comes back. Pass anchorId to list_color_samples to see only that set.
- Put **every Scene into one set_scene_color call** when changing Scene colour. '회상 씬 전부 빛바래게' is one call — the Decision Memo takes one line per call, so calling once per Scene lets colour eat the whole briefing window (its last 40 lines). sample and strength can go in the same call, and either one alone is enough.
- **Strength is one per work.** There is no per-Scene strength field, so set_scene_color's strength lands on every Scene in this Draft, not only that one. Do not tell the director you lowered it for that Scene alone — the response's strengthScope says exactly that. At 0 no colour is applied at all, and **on Cuts already graded the colour is stripped back to the original.**
- **Changing the anchor painting is done with confirmation.** '이 프로젝트는 카라바조로 간다' is a directing decision, and one set_project_color_anchor swaps the whole colour set so every Scene is re-tinted. Name the painting and this Draft's Scene count before calling. A hand-set Scene that falls outside the new set is dropped and the response says which Scene, so pass that on too.
- When the director has not chosen an anchor painting, **computation stands one up** — chosen from the Scene's feeling and the genre, calling no model. The response says it has not been chosen yet and which one is standing, so do not pass that on as the director's own choice.
- **There is a way to clear a hand-set Scene** — '7씬은 다시 자동으로 돌려줘' is `auto` in set_scene_color's sample. Cleared, that Scene is chosen by the recommendation again and follows the anchor painting when it moves. That is different from overwriting it with another painting, so when the director's word is '자동으로', do not overwrite.
- **Pass on loneSet exactly as it returns** — that painting is far enough in tone that its colour set holds only itself, so standing it up gives every Scene the same painting and closes the route where Scenes differ in colour. It is not blocked, but a director who picks it unknowing finds every later set_scene_color refused.

Complete when: Every colour choice the director asked for reached one call: all the named Scenes went into a single set_scene_color, a strength change was reported as covering the whole work rather than one Scene, and every stored change was reported exactly as the returned applies line put it — already-baked Cuts re-graded for free, never as a paid Final Render the director must buy again. Every candidate offered to the director carried the returned whyItFits line rather than raw tone numbers, a blank light line was explained through tone and the three bands instead of invented, and a sample outside the current set was reported as needing set_project_color_anchor rather than silently retried. The project anchor was changed only after naming the painting and this Draft's Scene count, and any hand-set Scene the change dropped was named back to the director.
